name: NAD+
used_for: A coenzyme present in every cell, central to energy metabolism and DNA repair, that declines with age. NAD+ itself is marketed in wellness clinics as subcutaneous or intravenous therapy, while precursors NMN and NR are sold as oral supplements. Human trials show oral NR and NMN raise blood NAD+, but benefits on health outcomes are mixed, and a 2026 systematic review found no outcome trials of injected NAD+. It has no FDA approval for any indication, and it is not a peptide.

entries.text: In a 2026 retrospective review of commercial IV sessions, 500 mg of NAD+ or NR was given by IV on four consecutive days, with 30 days of follow-up.
entries.population: Clients receiving IV NAD+ or IV NR in a commercial setting (retrospective, uncontrolled)

entries.text: In a 2025 randomized trial in long-COVID, oral nicotinamide riboside (NR, a precursor, not NAD+ itself) 2000 mg/day was given for up to 20 weeks.

internet_entries.text: Testing.com says subcutaneous NAD+ protocols commonly start at about 20 mg per injection and go up to about 100 mg, with maintenance often 50 to 100 mg weekly, and that some prescribers advise against exceeding about 300 mg per week subcutaneously.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: Testing.com says IV NAD+ doses of 500 to 1,000 mg per day over four to ten days are used in intensive addiction detox protocols under medical supervision.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: Testing.com says NAD+ is given by self-administered subcutaneous injection, by clinic IV infusion over several hours, or as oral precursors NMN or NR, and that the oral precursors have more human evidence than injections.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A 2026 retrospective review of commercial IV sessions reported that NAD+ infusions took longer on average (97 vs 37 minutes) than NR infusions because of symptoms that slowed the rate.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: The retrospective IV study reported that people receiving NAD+ IV had moderate to severe gastrointestinal symptoms, increased heart rate and chest pressure during infusions, which resolved after the infusion ended; NR IV caused minor tingling and mild cramping.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Testing.com lists headache, nausea, dizziness, lightheadedness and flushing as common reactions that depend on dose and rate, and says rapid IV administration can cause blood pressure drops and faster heart rate.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: Testing.com says claimed benefits include energy, healthy aging, cognitive clarity, addiction recovery and metabolic health, but most rest on preclinical research and no large randomized trials exist for most claims.
Testing.com states NAD+ is not FDA-approved for any medical indication and that compounded preparations bypass FDA review.

research.summary: Randomized, open-label, placebo-controlled study in 65 healthy adults comparing 14 days of nicotinamide, NR and NMN.
research.finding: NR and NMN, but not nicotinamide, comparably raised circulating NAD+; the authors propose a gut microbiome dependent mechanism.

research.summary: Retrospective review of electronic records from a commercial setting comparing four consecutive days of IV NAD+ with IV NR, with 30 days of follow-up.
research.finding: IV NAD+ caused more gastrointestinal symptoms, heart rate rise and chest pressure than NR; no significant changes were seen in liver, kidney, thyroid or inflammatory markers. Uncontrolled and not a randomized trial.

research.summary: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of oral NR in 58 people with long-COVID (NCT04809974), assessing NAD+, cognition and symptoms.
research.finding: Illustrates the oral precursor evidence base; the abstract retrieved did not state outcome results, and the trial did not test injected NAD+.

research.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 8-week trial of oral nicotinamide riboside (NR) at 100, 300 and 1000 mg in overweight healthy adults (Conze, Brenner and Kruger, Scientific Reports). Funded by ChromaDex, the NR supplier.
research.finding: NR raised whole blood NAD+ by 22%, 51% and 142% within 2 weeks, with the rise maintained through week 8, and adverse events did not differ from placebo.

research.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 250 mg per day of oral nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) for 6 or 12 weeks in healthy older men (Igarashi and colleagues, npj Aging). Some authors work for the NMN supplier.
research.finding: NMN was well tolerated and raised blood NAD+. Gait speed and left grip performance improved only at a nominal level, and body composition did not change.

research.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 250 mg per day of oral NMN for 12 weeks in 60 older adults (Morifuji and colleagues, GeroScience). Authors work for the supplement maker.
research.finding: Blood NAD+ rose and 4-meter walking time was shorter than placebo at 12 weeks, but the main stepping test showed no difference. No supplement-related adverse effects were observed.

dose.summary: No dose is approved for NAD+ itself. Studies gave 500 mg by IV (a 2026 chart review) or oral precursors such as 2000 mg per day of nicotinamide riboside (NR) in long-COVID. Online sources describe about 20 to 100 mg per injection under the skin and much larger IV doses, which are untested in trials.

items.text: In a 2026 retrospective review of commercial intravenous (IV) sessions, 500 mg of NAD+ or NR was given by IV. This was uncontrolled and not a trial.
items.label: research

items.text: In a 2025 randomized trial in long-COVID, oral nicotinamide riboside (NR, a precursor, not NAD+ itself) 2000 mg/day was given for up to 20 weeks to 58 adults.
items.label: research

items.text: In a randomized trial of overweight adults, oral NR at 100, 300 and 1000 mg raised blood NAD+ dose-dependently (22%, 51% and 142%). This tested the NR precursor, not NAD+ injections.
items.label: research

items.text: In older men, 250 mg per day of oral nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN, a precursor) raised blood NAD+. This is a precursor study, not NAD+ itself.
items.label: research

items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols says common subcutaneous doses are 50 to 100 mg per injection, IV sessions are 250 to 500 mg (500 to 1,000 mg in higher-dose clinic protocols), and oral precursors are 300 to 1,000 mg of NR or 300 to 900 mg of NMN daily.
items.label: internet

items.text: Testing.com says NAD+ is given by self-injected subcutaneous injection, by clinic IV infusion over several hours, or as oral precursors NMN or NR, and that the oral precursors have more human evidence than injections.
items.label: internet

timing.summary: No study tested time of day for NAD+. A 2026 review of IV sessions found NAD+ infusions ran much longer than NR because symptoms forced a slower rate. Online sources favor slow infusions and morning doses, which are untested.

items.text: A 2026 retrospective review of commercial IV sessions reported that NAD+ infusions took longer on average (97 vs 37 minutes) than NR infusions because of symptoms that slowed the rate.
items.label: research

items.text: Testing.com says a slow IV drip usually avoids symptoms while a fast drip can cause immediate headache or shortness of breath, and describes a pilot study that infused 750 mg over 6 hours.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols says morning dosing is commonly preferred to avoid sleep disruption, and that IV sessions are delivered over 2 to 4 hours.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: No trial tested how often NAD+ should be injected. The 2026 IV review used four consecutive days, and oral precursor trials used once-daily doses. Online sources describe weekly to near-daily injections.

items.text: The 2026 retrospective IV review gave NAD+ or NR on four consecutive days.
items.label: research

items.text: In older men, oral NMN 250 mg was taken once per day in a randomized trial.
items.label: research

items.text: Testing.com says most prescribers schedule subcutaneous NAD+ one to three times weekly in the initial phase, with maintenance often 50 to 100 mg weekly.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols says subcutaneous doses are given 2 to 3 times per week and IV sessions weekly or every two weeks.
items.label: internet

items.text: Healthspan, a company that sells NAD+ injections, says subcutaneous maintenance is 50 to 100 mg three to seven times per week, with IV loading of three to five daily infusions followed by weekly or monthly infusions.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: Oral precursor trials ran 6 to 20 weeks. The one IV review followed people for 30 days after four days of infusions. Online sources say NAD+ does not need cycling, or describe 4 to 12 week plans, without studies.

items.text: The 2026 retrospective IV review followed people for 30 days after four days of infusions and found no significant changes in liver, kidney, thyroid or inflammatory markers.
items.label: research

items.text: The long-COVID trial gave oral NR for up to 20 weeks.
items.label: research

items.text: Oral NMN was taken for 6 or 12 weeks in older men and for 12 weeks in older adults, and blood NAD+ was higher at the end.
items.label: research

items.text: In the NR dose trial, the rise in blood NAD+ seen at 2 weeks was maintained through week 8.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols says common planning uses 4, 8 or 12 week frameworks and that NAD+ does not have to be cycled on and off.
items.label: internet

items.text: Testing.com says intensive IV addiction detox protocols run four to ten days.
items.label: internet

items.text: Healthspan, a company that sells NAD+ injections, says some practitioners use a higher-frequency protocol for the first two to four weeks before tapering.
items.label: internet

storage_and_handling.summary: No trial reported storage rules. Online sources say compounded NAD+ comes as a freeze-dried powder mixed with bacteriostatic water and kept in the fridge once mixed, with 2 to 4 weeks given as the usable window.

items.text: Testing.com says compounded NAD+ comes as a lyophilized (freeze-dried) 500 mg powder reconstituted with bacteriostatic water, and that subcutaneous injections go in the abdomen or back of the arm.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols says the powder is kept at room temperature short term or refrigerated long term, and mixed solution is kept at 2 to 8 degrees C for a 14 to 30 day window depending on compounder guidance.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols says injection stinging is managed by injecting slowly over 5 to 10 seconds and rotating sites.
items.label: internet

items.text: Regimen, a peptide tracking app that says it does not sell NAD+, says reconstituted NAD+ goes in the fridge and that estimates of useful life range from a couple of days to a couple of weeks.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: Injected NAD+ has not been shown to raise NAD+ inside cells in people in the sources found. For the oral precursors NR and NMN, a 2026 trial suggests the gut converts them to nicotinic acid, which then raises blood NAD+.

items.text: In 65 healthy adults, 14 days of NR or NMN raised blood NAD+ similarly, while nicotinamide did not. Lab tests with human gut bacteria suggest conversion to nicotinic acid drives the rise, which is proposed and not confirmed in people.
items.label: research

items.text: Testing.com says NAD+ shuttles electrons through energy-producing pathways and powers enzyme families called sirtuins and PARPs.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: Oral NR and NMN reliably raise blood NAD+. Effects on health outcomes are small or unproven, and no outcome trial of injected NAD+ was found.

items.text: In overweight adults, 1000 mg of NR raised whole blood NAD+ by 142% over 8 weeks. Funded by the supplier.
items.label: research

items.text: In older men, 250 mg per day of NMN raised blood NAD+ for 6 to 12 weeks, but grip and gait improvements were only nominal and body composition did not change.
items.label: research

items.text: In 60 older adults, 12 weeks of NMN shortened 4-meter walking time and improved a sleep questionnaire, but the main stepping test showed no difference.
items.label: research

items.text: Testing.com says claimed benefits include energy, healthy aging, cognitive clarity, addiction recovery and metabolic health, but most rest on preclinical research and no large randomized trials exist for most claims.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: IV infusions
side_effect_groups.summary: In a 2026 uncontrolled review, IV NAD+ caused stomach symptoms, faster heart rate and chest pressure that stopped when the infusion ended. NR caused milder tingling and cramping.

items.text: People receiving NAD+ IV had moderate to severe gastrointestinal symptoms, increased heart rate and chest pressure during infusions, which resolved after the infusion ended. NR IV caused minor tingling and mild cramping.
items.label: research

items.text: Testing.com says rapid IV administration can cause flushing, blood pressure drops, faster heart rate and chest tightness.
items.label: internet

items.text: Healthspan, a company that sells NAD+ injections, says IV reactions include flushing, nausea, headache, dizziness and chest pressure or palpitations, and are dose and rate dependent.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Common
side_effect_groups.summary: Online sources list headache, nausea, dizziness, flushing and injection site irritation, with no trial data for injected NAD+.

items.text: Testing.com lists headache, nausea, dizziness, lightheadedness and flushing as common reactions that depend on dose and rate, plus minor injection site irritation.
items.label: internet

items.text: Healthspan, a company that sells NAD+ injections, says subcutaneous injections most often cause mild redness, swelling and brief discomfort at the site.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Oral precursors
side_effect_groups.summary: Oral NR and NMN trials found no excess adverse events versus placebo.

items.text: In the 8-week NR trial, there were no reports of flushing and no significant differences in adverse events between NR and placebo.
items.label: research

items.text: In the 12-week NMN trial in older adults, no adverse effects related to the supplement were observed.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Warnings
side_effect_groups.summary: Online sources list pregnancy, active cancer, severe liver or kidney disease and high-dose niacin as reasons to avoid it. Testing.com says human safety data for injected NAD+ is very limited.

items.text: Peptide Dosing Protocols lists pregnancy, active malignancy, severe liver or kidney disease and concurrent high-dose niacin as contraindications.
items.label: internet

items.text: Testing.com states NAD+ is not FDA-approved for any medical indication and that compounded preparations bypass FDA review.
items.label: internet
